title: Localization preserves projective dimension and finite global dimension
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset, $S^{-1}R$ the ring of fractions and, for an $R$-module $M$, $S^{-1}M$ the $S^{-1}R$-module of fractions $m/s$; let $n\ge0$. (1) If $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], then $S^{-1}M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$ over $S^{-1}R$. (2) If $R$ has global dimension $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], then $S^{-1}R$ has global dimension $\le n$; in particular, if $R$ has finite global dimension then so has $S^{-1}R$, with $\operatorname{gl.dim}S^{-1}R\le\operatorname{gl.dim}R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00O8 (lemma-localize-finite-gl-dim, line 26881), with its proof (localization is exact, Proposition 00CS; $S^{-1}P$ projective for $P$ projective, Lemma 05A3 ascend-properties-modules; $M'=S^{-1}M'$ for an $S^{-1}R$-module $M'$)
